title: Chicago Empire Room, Connie Haynes and other clippings
summary: Riddick names a friendly Indianapolis businessman and Connie Haynes, who got the band into the Empire Room.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: The L. W. Klein, the Gabriel Company. This was a very fine friend of mine, and a very wealthy man in Indianapolis, Indiana. Mm-hmm. And always, always, every time he came to New Orleans, always had me to his hotel suite, and his wife would love me.

Joe Reichman and Connie Haynes. That's the gal that got our band into the Empire Room in the Ballman House in Chicago. No, Connie Haynes. We can thank her for that. That was the only, that was the first jazz band that ever went as an actor.
Local 82, Eddie Grady. I don't know who he is. I don't know. Charlie Ben-Oni. I don't know who he is.
I wonder if he's kin to Nick. No. Nick Ben-Oni. I don't know.
But you know Nick. Oh, very well. Played many, many times. I got a picture with Nick Ben-Oni playing in the same band. Red Nichols. Yeah, that's, that's...
Sidney Boucher. That's Look Magazine. And that's that same article. I'll give it a minute. Look. Jazz. That's that same article. Look. Jazz. 된된된
